subject: Logic
title: The Gambler's Fallacy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Gambler's Fallacy.

hook.text: A roulette wheel hits red ten times straight. "Black is due!" The wheel disagrees.

buildup.text: The gambler's fallacy assumes that past random events affect future ones. They don't—each spin is fresh.

discovery.text: In 1913 at Monte Carlo, black hit 26 times in a row. Gamblers lost millions betting on red.

twist.text: The fallacy feels rational. Our pattern-seeking brains see streaks and demand balance that doesn't exist.

climax.text: Independent events have no memory. A coin doesn't know—or care—what happened last flip.

quiz.question: What does the gambler's fallacy incorrectly assume?
options: Past random events influence future ones
